cards.text: King Hezekiah of Judah sends word throughout all Israel and Judah, and he even writes letters to Ephraim and Manasseh. He's inviting them all to keep the Passover of the LORD. Friend, this man is inviting the WHOLE country, and I get nervous inviting over one baker.

cards.question: Hezekiah is inviting everybody to keep the Passover. Where does he want them to come?

answers.text: The house of the LORD in Jerusalem

cards.text: One problem. The Passover has a regular time, and this year they missed it.

cards.question: Since they missed the regular time, the king, his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem decide to keep the Passover in the ___ month.
Why couldn't Judah keep the Passover at the regular time?

answers.text: Not enough priests had consecrated themselves
The temple doors were still locked up
The king was away fighting a war

cards.question: The plan to keep the Passover in the second month pleases the king and the whole assembly.

cards.text: So they make it official: a proclamation goes all through Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, calling the people to Jerusalem for the Passover. It hadn't been kept in great numbers the way it was written.
The couriers head out across Israel and Judah carrying letters from the king and his officials. No group chat, no email, friend, just feet, and I BET those feet hurt.

cards.question: The king's letter calls the children of Israel to return to the LORD, so that He may return to them.
The king's letter speaks to the people who remain, the ones who escaped the grasp of the kings of ___.

cards.text: Then the letter gets honest. Don't be like your fathers and brothers who were unfaithful to the LORD, and don't stiffen your necks the way they did.

cards.question: Instead of stiffening their necks, what does the king's letter tell the people to do?

answers.text: Submit to the LORD and come to His sanctuary
Build an altar to the LORD in their own town
Wait at home until a prophet comes to them

cards.question: The king's letter says that even if the people return to the LORD, their captured brothers and sons are gone for good.
The king's letter promises the LORD won't turn His face away if they come back. Why can they count on that?

answers.text: He owes their fathers a debt

cards.text: So the couriers go city to city through Ephraim and Manasseh, all the way to Zebulun, carrying a personal invitation from the KING. If that had landed in my junk drawer, I'd have read it out loud every single night to the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, whether they were listening or not.

cards.question: How do the people in Ephraim, Manasseh and Zebulun treat the king's couriers? They ___ and ___ them.
Some people from Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humble themselves and come to Jerusalem.

cards.text: Mocked up north, but now look at Judah. The power of God is on the people there.

cards.question: What does the power of God give the people of Judah?

answers.text: One heart to obey the king's command
Gold to fill the house of the LORD

cards.text: In the second month, a VERY great assembly gathers in Jerusalem for the Feast of Unleavened Bread. And then the GUESTS start cleaning up, friend, the guests, which is exactly the kind of crowd I want in my bakery.

cards.question: Before the feast, what does the great crowd in Jerusalem clear out of the city?

answers.text: The altars and the incense altars
The money changers and their tables
The golden calves and their shrines

cards.question: The crowd throws those altars out of Jerusalem and into the ___ Valley.

cards.text: On the fourteenth day of the second month, they slaughter the Passover lamb. Then something hits the priests and Levites.

cards.question: The Passover lamb is slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the second month. How do the priests and Levites feel?

cards.text: Then they consecrate themselves and bring burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.

The priests and Levites stand at their prescribed posts by the Law of Moses the man of God, and the priests splatter the blood the Levites hand them. Smooth handoff, no fumbles, which is more than I can say for my first week packing cookie boxes with a mustache.
Problem: many in the crowd hadn't consecrated themselves. So the Levites slaughter the Passover lambs for every unclean person, like one coworker covering EVERYBODY'S shift at once.

cards.question: Many people from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun hadn't purified themselves, so they sit out the Passover meal.

cards.text: Nope, they ate the Passover anyway, contrary to what was written. Ohhh, friend. Now what's the KING gonna do about that?

cards.question: Many people ate the Passover without purifying themselves. What does King Hezekiah do?

answers.text: He speaks up for them before the LORD
He sends them away from Jerusalem
He bars them from the temple

cards.question: Hezekiah speaks up for the people who ate without being purified, saying, "May the LORD, who is good, provide atonement for everyone…" Everyone who does what?

answers.text: Sets his heart on seeking God
Brings the biggest offering to God
Was born in the land of Judah

cards.question: After Hezekiah intercedes, the LORD hears him and heals the people.

cards.text: The people are healed, and now the Feast of Unleavened Bread runs seven days with great joy, the Levites and priests praising the LORD day after day with LOUD instruments. After years of quiet in a junk drawer, friend, LOUD is my favorite kind of music.

cards.question: What does King Hezekiah do for the Levites who serve skillfully before the LORD?

cards.text: For seven days they eat their assigned portion, sacrifice peace offerings and give thanks to the LORD, the God of their fathers. Then the whole assembly makes a decision.

cards.question: The feast has run seven days. Then the whole assembly agrees to observe ___ more days.

cards.text: Hezekiah gives a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, the officials give a thousand bulls and TEN THOUSAND sheep, and a great number of priests consecrate themselves. Friend, the most I've ever handed out at once is a double scoop of sprinkles, and I STILL felt like a big shot.

cards.question: Only the people of Judah get to rejoice, and the foreigners are left out.

cards.text: So there's great rejoicing in Jerusalem. Nothing like it in a long, LONG time.

cards.question: Nothing like this had happened in Jerusalem since the days of ___ son of David king of Israel.
To close out the feast, the priests and Levites stand to bless the people. What happens to their prayer?

answers.text: It reaches God's holy dwelling in heaven
The king has it written in his records
The people repeat it all through the night

cards.text: And that's where we pause, friend. The oven's still warm on Hezekiah's story, and it is NOT done baking.

findings.problem: The fill-in-the-blank cards repeatedly require guesses at unrevealed details rather than inferences from the setup. For example, the earlier cards give no way to reason out Assyria (stop 1 card 10), scorn and mock (stop 1 card 16), Kidron (stop 2 card 3), or Solomon (stop 3 card 8). The second month and the length of the extension likewise depend on guessing (stop 1 card 4 and stop 3 card 4).

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Verse 3 gives two reasons the Passover could not be kept at the regular time: too few priests had consecrated themselves, and the people had not gathered in Jerusalem. The correct option names only the first reason, and no other card tells the second, leaving the explanation of the delay incomplete.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "Mocked up north" retells the response in verse 10, but the card cites only verse 12. The citation does not cover all the passage content the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The correct answer, "Sets his heart on seeking God," comes from verse 19. Verse 18 supplies the quotation and setup in the question, but the choice card's citation should be only 2 Chronicles 30:19, not 2 Chronicles 30:18-19.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The opening clause, "The people are healed," retells verse 20, but the card cites only verse 21. Either that recap needs to be removed or the citation must account for the verse actually used.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
